sections.name: PriorityMatrix
sections.title: Weights panel, grid and top-ten list
sections.what: Shows sliders for each factor with its percentage share, a preset picker, and a reset button. Re-sorts all signals by weighted score, places each on an impact versus actionability grid with four labelled quadrants, and lists the top ten with arrows that show how far each moved against the default ranking.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets triage change what counts as important while still showing how that differs from the default.
sections.watch_out: Quadrant boundaries are fixed at 3 on a 1 to 5 scale, so a change in that scale would move signals between quadrants.

summary: Ranks opportunity signals using user-set weights and places them on an impact versus actionability grid so users can decide what to pursue first.
purpose: Helps a team triage signals by letting them decide what matters most and see the result at a glance.
why: Likely reason: different teams weigh factors differently, so the weights are adjustable, and the default ranking is kept so the app can show how each signal moved.
how: Shows sliders for each factor and their percentage share, and presets. Scores all signals with the current weights, sorts them, places each on a grid by impact and actionability, counts signals in four labelled quadrants, and lists the top ten with movement arrows against the default ranking.
inputs: A list of signals, the current weights, a callback to change the weights, a callback to open a signal, and a flag for demo mode.
outputs: A weights panel, a grid of numbered dots and quadrant counts, and a ranked list of the top ten. Clicking any signal opens it.
risks: Scores are for triage only and are not financial estimates. Quadrant lines are fixed at 3 on a 1 to 5 scale. If all weights are set to zero, the percentages show zero.
debug: If ranking looks wrong, check the weights and the preset in use, then the scoring rules in the priority module. If dots sit in the wrong place, check the impact and actionability values for the signal. If the reset button stays disabled, weights may already match the defaults.
